claim.quote: The results constitute the first observation of direct photons in ultrarelativistic heavy-ion collisions which could be significant for diagnosis of quark gluon plasma formation.

date.note: Preprint date; the WA98 website records publication in Phys. Rev. Lett. 85 (2000) 3595.

name: WA98 first observation of direct photons in central Pb+Pb collisions

summary.plain: WA98 measured photons from central lead-lead collisions at 158 GeV per nucleon and, after subtracting those from particle decays, found a direct-photon signal above 1.5 GeV/c, the first such observation in ultrarelativistic heavy-ion collisions.
summary.technical: Direct-photon invariant yield in central 208Pb+208Pb collisions at 158A GeV extracted as a function of transverse momentum for 0.5 < pT < 4 GeV/c; a significant signal compared with statistical and systematic errors is seen at pT > 1.5 GeV/c (points at lower pT are upper limits).

title: Observation of Direct Photons in Central 158 A GeV 208Pb+208Pb Collisions
why_it_matters: Direct photons escape the collision zone without further interaction, so they probe the hot early stage; the 2026 SPS review says the excess showed high temperatures (up to 200 MeV) were reached, consistent with QGP formation.
